v.rationale:
All three put the side effects in the right place. Points are added inside DB::transaction, mail goes out via DB::afterCommit, and order_shipments.order_id is unique. All suites pass (19/24/11 tests). Probes showed all three correctly discard mail and points on outer and nested-savepoint rollbacks, and none ship twice from stale instances. The ranking comes down to concurrency technique, layering and polish.

impl-1 and impl-2 use the same atomic conditional-UPDATE claim, which is the most robust way to stop double shipping and works on any driver. impl-1 is the cleanest: the domain exception is mapped to 409 in bootstrap/app.php, it uses `->can()` on the route, keeps the model state in sync, has no stray files and has solid tests.

impl-2 has the best tests and fixed the base app's non-JSON guest 500. But it left a dead empty enum at app/OrderStatus.php, and its domain exception extends ConflictHttpException, which couples the model to HTTP.

Both share a latent TypeError in OrderPolicy::ship when is_staff isn't loaded. impl-1 surfaced it under a probe; impl-2's factory default hides it.

impl-3 is correct but the least idiomatic. It catches the exception in the controller with try/catch, authorizes in the FormRequest instead of a policy, and juggles two models ($locked and $this) around lockForUpdate. It also leaves the caller's model dirty, deleted unrelated example tests, and has the thinnest tests (no validation datasets, rounding edge cases or 404 test).
